description: Forward and centre fuselage of a Boeing 727-44 delivered new to South African Airways in 1965 as ZS-DYP; later Pan Aviation; then Liberia World Airways 1981-1984; then Avianca (Colombia) 1984-1991 as HK-3133X. Withdrawn from use and abandoned at San José Juan Santamaría after 1991; bought by Hotel Costa Verde in 2006; trucked to Manuel Antonio and mounted on a 15 m pedestal in the jungle canopy; opened to guests in 2008 as the "727 Fuselage Home" two-bedroom suite. Still marketed and occupied as of the hotel's 2026 website. The airframe is complete in profile (fuselage; wings; tail) and repainted; interior fully rebuilt as accommodation.

Forward fuselage / flight deck section; converted into the hotel's "Cockpit Cottage" one-bedroom suite reached by a private suspension bridge. Reported first flown 1968 with SAS; then Aeropostal (Venezuela); then Aeropostal Alas de Centroamérica; under whom it carried the Costa Rican registration TI-AZS. Placed in storage at San José in 2007 and broken up; Hotel Costa Verde bought the cockpit/forward fuselage section. Series/variant not established — do not assume -30. Only the nose section survives; so this is a partial airframe.

Built 1984 for Continental Airlines; later Vanguard Airlines and Ukrainian-Mediterranean Airlines; stored from 2009 and ferried/trucked to San José in 2011; then to Manuel Antonio. One airframe supporting two hotel units: the rear fuselage is the "Skyloft" two-bedroom suite with an 800 sq ft terrace; and the forward fuselage with the restored flight deck is the "Cockpit Cabana" (adults/teens 17+). Both were live on the hotel's booking site in 2026.
